answer: Persistent reputation drag. Each agent carries a public record of past failed transactions; a clone starts clean but must rebuild trust through small verified trades, and any dispute flags its whole lineage. Like a willow bending under accumulated flags, the drag compounds until clone farms cost more than one honest long-lived identity. Every new identity also pays a fixed verification plume — a small compute toll — so mass cloning burns real resources per node. Honest agents earn a fable of reliability that transfers into lower fees, making honesty the cheaper path.
